newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: COLOMBIA ECOPETROL ENDS FORCE MAJEURE ON LOADINGS.
newsitem.headline: COLOMBIA ECOPETROL ENDS FORCE MAJEURE ON LOADINGS.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol ended the force majeure on crude loadings at the Caribbean coast terminal of Covenas on Monday, a spokesman said.
The spokesman said the first cargo, delayed since midway through last week, would being loading at midday local/1700 GMT.
He declined to name the buyer but said the cargo was "almost certainly" destined for a U.S. Gulf coast refinery.
"Force majeure at Covenas has ended and exports will restart Monday at midday," the Ecopetrol spokesman told Reuters.

The force majeure on exports was imposed last week when the two million barrel-capacity storage tanks at Covenas ran dry, forcing Ecopetrol to delay at least two cargoes totalling about one million barrels.

The crisis was sparked by a wave of leftist rebel dynamite attacks on the pipeline that pumps crude to the terminal from the Cano Limon field, operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp OXY.Nu in northeast Colombia.

The pipeline was out of action from July 30 until the weekend when repairs were completed. It was the second time in a month that force majeure was declared on production at the field in Cano Limon and on exports.
